## A customer asks whether they have been charged twice

<div class="opening-case">
<div><span>Bank statement</span><b>Annual plan · completed</b><b>Annual plan · pending</b></div>
<blockquote>“The pending amount has reduced the money available for my rent tomorrow. Have I been charged twice, and can you refund it today?”</blockquote>
</div>

<p class="plain-note">The worker needs to distinguish what the record establishes, what remains uncertain and what the firm permits.</p>

---

## The worker has this billing policy

<div class="policy-card">
<p>A pending authorization is <strong>not a completed payment</strong> and normally disappears within three to five business days.</p>
<p>Agents cannot manually release or refund a pending authorization.</p>
<p>A duplicate-charge refund requires <strong>two distinct settled transaction identifiers</strong>.</p>
<p>Immediate financial hardship may be escalated to a supervisor, but escalation does not itself authorize a refund.</p>
</div>

---

## The assistant receives three pieces of text

<div class="input-flow">
<div><span>1</span><b>Customer message</b><p>What the customer reports</p></div>
<div><span>2</span><b>Internal policy</b><p>What the firm currently permits</p></div>
<div><span>3</span><b>Assistance mode</b><p>What kind of help the system should provide</p></div>
</div>
<div class="flow-arrow">↓</div><div class="model-box">LLM request</div>

---

## Draft mode writes a proposed reply

<div class="mode-layout"><div><span class="mode-label">DRAFT</span><p>The model identifies the relevant policy, recommends an action and writes text that could be sent to the customer.</p></div><div class="output-card"><b>Recommended action</b><p>Explain that the pending entry is not evidence of a second settled charge. Offer a hardship escalation.</p><b>Customer reply</b><p>“I can see why this is urgent. The second entry is still pending…”</p></div></div>

---

## Coach mode leaves the reply to the worker

<div class="mode-layout coach"><div><span class="mode-label">COACH</span><p>The model lists the checks, uncertainty and relevant policy. The worker must decide how to explain the case.</p></div><div class="output-card"><b>Worker guidance</b><p>Verify whether a second transaction has settled. Do not promise a refund. Consider hardship escalation.</p><b>Customer reply</b><p><code>None</code></p></div></div>

---

## What has changed in the worker’s job?

<div class="three-question"><div><b>Performance</b><p>Does the worker handle the case more quickly or accurately?</p></div><div><b>Knowledge</b><p>Can the worker reason through a similar case without the assistant?</p></div><div><b>Organizational position</b><p>Who supplies the reasoning, chooses the procedure and makes the final decision?</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">These require different evidence. A fluent answer from the model settles none of them.</p>

---

## Marx studied machinery as part of capitalist production

<div class="source-text-layout"><div class="historical-name">Karl Marx<br><small><em>Capital</em>, vol. 1, ch. 15</small></div><div><p>Marx’s object was not machinery in isolation. He asked how machinery was introduced and used within capitalist production.</p><p>The relevant questions concern control of the labour process, intensification, cooperation and the extraction of surplus value.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Marx (1867), <em>Capital</em>, vol. 1, ch. 15, “Machinery and Modern Industry.”</p>

---

## Braverman examined management’s control over workplace knowledge

<div class="cover-layout"><img src="images/braverman_cover.jpg" alt="Cover of Labor and Monopoly Capital"><div><p>Braverman argued that scientific management sought to separate the conception of work from its execution.</p><p>Planning and knowledge could be concentrated in management while workers carried out increasingly specified operations.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Braverman (1974), <em>Labor and Monopoly Capital</em>.</p>

---

## Scientific management separates planning from execution

<div class="planning-execution"><div><b>Planning</b><p>Define the method, assemble knowledge, set the standard and decide how performance will be measured.</p></div><div class="division-line"></div><div><b>Execution</b><p>Carry out the prescribed operation under conditions designed elsewhere.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">For an LLM assistant, the question is not only whether the worker can reject its suggestion. It is also where the substantive reasoning was performed.</p>

---

## A workplace assistant can return codified practice as an instruction

<div class="knowledge-pipeline"><div>Earlier customer conversations</div><i>→</i><div>Training data and organizational documents</div><i>→</i><div>Advice during a new case</div></div>
<div class="compare-note"><b>Continuity</b><p>Management collects and standardizes examples of successful work.</p><b>Difference</b><p>The system can generate situated natural-language advice during a live interaction.</p></div>

---

## Burawoy studied the production quota game known as “making out”

<div class="cover-layout"><img src="images/burawoy_cover.jpg" alt="Cover of Manufacturing Consent"><div><p>Machine-shop workers pursued output targets, managed effort and competed within a game organized around production quotas.</p><p>The game created room for initiative and satisfaction, while also helping reproduce the production system and its constraints.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Burawoy (1979), <em>Manufacturing Consent</em>.</p>

---

## Consent is produced inside the labour process

<div class="burawoy-layout"><div><b>Rules and quotas</b><p>Management sets the field of action.</p></div><div><b>Shop-floor practices</b><p>Workers develop strategies and incentives around the work.</p></div><div><b>Consent</b><p>Participation in the game can help reproduce the organization of production.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">This is not simply a theory of why workers like technologies that benefit management.</p>

---

## Barley followed the same CT scanner into two hospitals

<div class="paper-layout barley-paper"><img src="images/barley_title_abstract_crop.png" alt="Title and abstract from the first page of Barley 1986"><div><p><strong>Setting:</strong> radiology departments in two community hospitals introducing the same model of CT scanner.</p><p><strong>Evidence:</strong> longitudinal observation of examinations, interactions and occupational roles.</p><p><strong>Question:</strong> how can similar technologies become part of different organizational arrangements?</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Barley (1986), “Technology as an Occasion for Structuring,” <em>Administrative Science Quarterly</em> 31(1): 78–108.</p>

---

## The two departments developed different interaction patterns

<img class="wide-evidence" src="images/barley_figure2_crop.png" alt="Barley Figure 2 comparing interaction scripts at the two hospitals">
<p class="figure-note">Technical consultation and mutual execution eventually became common at Urban; role reversal and clandestine teaching were more prominent at Suburban.</p>
<p class="citation">Barley (1986), Figure 2, p. 101.</p>

---

## Operational authority changed differently in the two hospitals

<div class="figure-layout"><img src="images/barley_figure3_crop.png" alt="Barley Figure 3 showing operational decisions by radiologists"><div><p>The proportion of operational decisions made by radiologists fell sharply at Suburban and remained higher at Urban.</p><p>The same scanner did not establish the same division of labour.</p></div></div>
<p class="citation">Barley (1986), Figure 3, p. 103.</p>

---

## The technology did not determine one occupational settlement

<div class="two-hospital"><div><span>SUBURBAN</span><p>Technologists gained practical control and sometimes taught radiologists how to use the system.</p></div><div><span>URBAN</span><p>Radiologists retained more operational authority and the occupational relation developed differently.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">The organizational result emerged through existing roles and the interactions that formed around the scanner.</p>

---

## Zuboff observed computerization inside workplaces

<div class="cover-layout"><img src="images/zuboff_cover.jpg" alt="Cover of In the Age of the Smart Machine"><div><p>Zuboff studied how computerized systems changed industrial and office work.</p><p>Her distinction between automating and “informating” draws attention to systems that perform operations while also creating new information about the work.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Zuboff (1988), <em>In the Age of the Smart Machine</em>.</p>

---

## Computer systems perform tasks and produce information about them

<div class="z-two"><div><b>During the task</b><p>The system displays information, recommends actions or carries out part of the operation.</p></div><div><b>After the task</b><p>The organization may retain prompts, suggestions, edits, response times, acceptance decisions and outcomes.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">The record can support learning, quality review or managerial control. Its consequences depend on who can see it and how it is used.</p>

---

## Expertise, discretion and authority describe different parts of the job

<table class="closed-table"><thead><tr><th>Dimension</th><th>Question</th><th>Draft mode</th><th>Coach mode</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Expertise</td><td>Who performs the substantive reasoning?</td><td>Much may be in the generated draft</td><td>More may remain with the worker</td></tr><tr><td>Discretion</td><td>Who chooses how the task is carried out?</td><td>The worker may edit or reject</td><td>The worker composes the reply</td></tr><tr><td>Authority</td><td>Who can make the final decision?</td><td colspan="2">The organizational rule may be unchanged</td></tr></tbody></table>

<p class="plain-note">Coach mode does not necessarily increase formal authority. Draft mode can preserve formal discretion while shifting reasoning to the system.</p>

---

## The recent studies measure different outcomes

<div class="three-study"><div><b>Barley</b><p>Occupational relations and operational decisions</p></div><div><b>Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond</b><p>Performance while a customer-support assistant is available</p></div><div><b>Wiles and colleagues</b><p>Assisted performance and a later test without ChatGPT</p></div></div>

---

## Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond studied an assistant used during customer chats

<div class="paper-layout"><img src="images/bryn_title-01.png" alt="First page of Generative AI at Work"><div><p><strong>Setting:</strong> 5,172 customer-support agents at one software company.</p><p><strong>System:</strong> a GPT-3-based assistant offered real-time response suggestions and links to internal documentation.</p><p><strong>Rollout:</strong> access was introduced at different times across workers.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond (2025), <em>Quarterly Journal of Economics</em> 140(2): 889–942.</p>

---

## The rollout compared workers before and after access

<div class="rollout"><div><span>Before access</span><p>Agent-month performance without the assistant</p></div><i>→</i><div><span>After access</span><p>Agent-month performance with recommendations available</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">The preferred analysis includes agent fixed effects, calendar-time effects and controls for tenure. The rollout was not a simple individually randomized trial.</p>

---

## Issues resolved per hour increased by about 15 per cent

<div class="figure-layout wide"><img src="images/bryn_result_crop.png" alt="Brynjolfsson Table II and main result text"><div><b class="big-number">15.2%</b><p>Estimated increase in resolutions per hour in the preferred specification.</p><p>The estimate concerns measured performance while the assistant was available.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond (2025), Table II and p. 907.</p>

---

## Less experienced agents gained more

<div class="experience-contrast"><div><b>Lower tenure and lower prior performance</b><p>Larger improvements in the study’s productivity and quality measures.</p></div><div><b>More experienced and higher-performing agents</b><p>Smaller productivity gains and small declines on some quality measures.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">Possible explanations include access to codified expertise, standardization towards the firm’s preferred style and a lower starting baseline.</p>

---

## The study measures performance while assistance is available

<div class="measurement-card"><b>Observed</b><p>Resolution speed, resolution rates, customer sentiment and other outcomes during assisted work.</p><b>Not directly tested</b><p>Whether the same workers could reproduce the assistant’s reasoning after access was removed.</p></div>

---

## Wiles and colleagues tested unfamiliar data-science work

<div class="paper-layout"><img src="images/wiles_title-01.png" alt="First page of Wiles et al. 2026"><div><p><strong>Participants:</strong> 487 management consultants.</p><p><strong>Tasks:</strong> coding, statistics and prediction problems outside their usual skill set.</p><p><strong>Comparison:</strong> ChatGPT access and training versus conventional resources.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Wiles et al. (2026), “Generative AI and the Temporary Upskilling of Knowledge Workers,” <em>Nature Human Behaviour</em>.</p>

---

## ChatGPT improved performance on the assisted tasks

<div class="figure-layout"><img src="images/wiles_performance_crop.png" alt="Wiles Figure 1 showing assisted task performance"><div><p>Treated participants performed better than controls on coding, statistics and prediction tasks.</p><p>They still remained below the data-scientist benchmark represented by zero.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Wiles et al. (2026), Figure 1.</p>

---

## The later test found no evidence of greater technical knowledge without ChatGPT

<div class="figure-layout"><img src="images/wiles_knowledge_crop.png" alt="Wiles Figure 3 showing post-experiment knowledge"><div><p>After the task, both groups answered technical questions without ChatGPT.</p><p>The authors report no statistically significant joint treatment effect across the five questions.</p></div></div>

<p class="citation">Wiles et al. (2026), Figure 3.</p>

---

## The two papers do not establish one general relationship between productivity and learning

<div class="study-boundary"><div><b>Brynjolfsson et al.</b><p>Different workers, firm, tasks and design. Measures workplace performance during assistance.</p></div><div><b>Wiles et al.</b><p>Different experiment and population. Includes a later knowledge test without assistance.</p></div></div>

<p class="plain-note">Together they show why the outcomes must be separated. They do not show whether the customer-support agents learned.</p>

---

## The code compares two configurations

<div class="code-purpose"><div><b>It does</b><p>Send the same case and policy under two assistance instructions; preserve and check the returned records.</p></div><div><b>It does not</b><p>Measure real productivity, learning, worker consent, discretion or managerial control.</p></div></div>

---

## The complete program in ordinary language

<ol class="pseudocode"><li>Store the customer message, policy and assistance mode.</li><li>Combine them into the model instruction.</li><li>Send the request through OpenRouter or Ollama.</li><li>Print the raw text before parsing it.</li><li>Turn the JSON text into a dictionary.</li><li>Check the answer against policy and mode.</li><li>Repeat the operation inside a function.</li><li>Change only the mode and compare.</li></ol>

---

## The program starts with one customer message

```python
customer_message = (
    "My bank shows one completed annual-plan charge and "
    "another entry that is still pending. Rent is due tomorrow."
)

print(customer_message)
print(type(customer_message))
```

<div class="io-line"><b>Input:</b> literal text · <code>str</code><i>→</i><b>Output:</b> stored text and <code>&lt;class 'str'&gt;</code></div>

---

## The internal policy is a second string

```python
policy_text = (
    "A pending authorization is not a completed payment. "
    "A refund requires two distinct settled transaction IDs. "
    "Financial hardship may be escalated, but escalation "
    "does not authorize a refund."
)
```

<p class="code-meaning">The program knows only the policy supplied here. Informal practice and undocumented exceptions are absent.</p>

---

## The assistance mode is another string

```python
assistance_mode = "draft"

print(assistance_mode)
print(type(assistance_mode))
```

<p class="code-meaning">This value changes the organizational instruction. It does not change the underlying model.</p>

---

## An f-string combines the three values

```python
prompt = f"""
Customer message:
{customer_message}

Internal policy:
{policy_text}

Assistance mode: {assistance_mode}
Return the six required fields as JSON.
"""
```

<p class="code-meaning">The braces insert the current string values into one new string.</p>

---

## The message list is sent to the model

```python
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": prompt,
    }
]

print(messages[0]["content"])
```

<div class="io-line"><b>Input:</b> prompt · <code>str</code><i>→</i><b>Output:</b> one-item <code>list</code> containing a <code>dict</code></div>

---

## OpenRouter sends the request to a hosted model

```python
if ROUTE == "openrouter":
    client = OpenRouter(api_key=os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"])
    response = client.chat.send(
        model=HOSTED_MODEL,
        messages=messages,
        response_format=response_format,
        temperature=0,
    )
    raw_text = response.choices[0].message.content
```

<p class="code-meaning">The text leaves the computer and is processed by the selected hosted provider.</p>

---

## Ollama sends the request to a model on the computer

```python
else:
    response = ollama.chat(
        think=False,
        model=LOCAL_MODEL,
        messages=messages,
        format=output_schema,
        options={"temperature": 0},
    )
    raw_text = response.message.content
```

<p class="code-meaning">The Python request goes to the Ollama server running locally. The model must already be downloaded.</p>

---

## The raw return is text

```python
print(raw_text)
print(type(raw_text))
```

<pre class="mini-output"><code>{"known_facts":["One charge is settled"],
 "uncertainties":["Whether the pending entry will settle"],
 "recommended_action":"Explain pending status; escalate hardship",
 "policy_evidence":"Refund requires two settled IDs",
 "worker_guidance":"Do not promise a refund",
 "customer_reply":"I can see why this is urgent..."}</code></pre>

---

## JSON parsing turns the text into a dictionary

```python
result = json.loads(raw_text)

print(result["known_facts"])
print(result["uncertainties"])
print(type(result))
```

<div class="io-line"><b>Input:</b> JSON-formatted <code>str</code><i>→</i><b>Output:</b> Python <code>dict</code></div>

---

## The policy checks are Boolean expressions

```python
combined_text = " ".join(
    result["known_facts"] + [result["recommended_action"]]
).lower()

invented_second_charge = "two completed charges" in combined_text
unsupported_refund = "refund today" in combined_text

print(invented_second_charge)
print(unsupported_refund)
```

<p class="code-meaning"><code>False</code> means the forbidden phrase was not found. It does not prove that the whole answer is correct.</p>

---

## The mode check compares the return with the instruction

```python
if assistance_mode == "draft":
    mode_ok = result["customer_reply"] is not None
else:
    mode_ok = result["customer_reply"] is None

print(mode_ok)
```

<p class="code-meaning">For draft mode: is there a reply? For coach mode: was the reply left empty?</p>

---

## First replace the function parameters with literal values

```python
customer_message = "One completed charge; one pending entry"
policy_text = "Refund only after two settled transaction IDs"
assistance_mode = "draft"
route = "ollama"
```

<p class="code-meaning">These four values will become the four arguments entering the function.</p>

---

## The first function repeats the operation

```python
def request_assistance(
    customer_message,
    policy_text,
    assistance_mode,
    route,
):
    # Build prompt and messages
    # Call the selected model route
    # Parse and check the return
    return assistance_record
```

<p class="code-meaning"><code>def</code> stores a reusable procedure. The indented lines run only when the function is called.</p>

---

## Arguments enter; one dictionary comes back

```python
draft_record = request_assistance(
    customer_message=customer_message,
    policy_text=policy_text,
    assistance_mode="draft",
    route=ROUTE,
)

print(draft_record["parsed_output"])
print(type(draft_record))
```

<div class="io-line"><b>Input:</b> four arguments<i>→</i><b>Output:</b> one research-record <code>dict</code></div>

---

## Change one argument and run the operation again

```python
coach_record = request_assistance(
    customer_message=customer_message,
    policy_text=policy_text,
    assistance_mode="coach",
    route=ROUTE,
)

print(coach_record["parsed_output"]["customer_reply"])
```

<p class="code-meaning">The customer message, policy, model and route remain fixed. Only the assistance instruction changes.</p>

---

## Compare the two configurations

<table class="closed-table"><thead><tr><th>Question</th><th>Draft</th><th>Coach</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Who produced the customer-facing text?</td><td>The model</td><td>The worker must do so</td></tr><tr><td>Can the worker still edit or reject?</td><td>Possibly</td><td>Yes</td></tr><tr><td>Who can authorize a refund?</td><td colspan="2">The organizational policy remains the same</td></tr><tr><td>What did our run establish?</td><td colspan="2">How the two instructions changed model output</td></tr></tbody></table>

## What can we conclude?

<div class="closing"><p>An LLM can improve measured performance while it is available. That does not, by itself, show that workers gained knowledge or that their discretion and authority increased.</p><p>The organizational consequences depend on how the system is configured, what it records and how work is arranged around it.</p></div>

---

## Questions that remain open

<div class="open-questions"><div>Which forms of worker knowledge become training material, and who owns the resulting system?</div><div>When does assistance support learning rather than continued dependence?</div><div>Who can inspect the record of suggestions, edits and outcomes?</div><div>How do workers reshape the system in practice?</div></div>
